extracted.intended_audience: research PIs (tenured/tenure-track or equivalent) in mathematics, physics, and computer science applying to the Simons Foundation MPS Targeted Grants program
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and requirements for preparing and submitting a Letter of Intent and, if invited, a full proposal to the Simons Foundation Mathematics & Physical Sciences Targeted Grants program. Covers eligibility, allowable costs, application formatting, SAM submission, and required attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose / project suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: The program is intended to support high-risk theoretical mathematics, physics and computer science projects of exceptional promise and scientific importance on a case-by-case basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While emphasis is on theory, projects with some experimental components may be considered. There are no fixed guidelines, but 'projects at the single- or few-PI scale that might be funded by federal agencies would not normally be considered under the Targeted Grants in MPS program.' The LOI stage is used to assess suitability and novelty; the foundation cannot provide advance guidance on potential proposals due to volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding duration and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Targeted Grant in MPS program provides funding for up to five years. The funding level and duration is flexible and should be appropriate based on the type of support requested in the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no recommended or assumed funding level for this program. In the event of budgetary or other considerations, SF reserves the right to refer an application to SFI for consideration and funding; SFI recipients are subject to SF Policies and Procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable expenses (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowable expenses include summer salary (subject to limitations), domestic or international travel, salary support for staff/postdocs/students, support for visitors and collaborators, conferences/working meetings, research equipment/experiments/computations/supplies, publication expenses and professional membership dues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists specific allowable categories in detail (see summer salary policy and travel/visitors/conferences). Expenses must be directly related to the research. Applicants should consult the Simons Foundation grant policies for further guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summer salary policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to one month of summer salary and related benefits per year is allowable for the PI and any co-Investigator(s). For scientists at non-U.S. universities on 12-month salaries, PIs may request up to 1/12 of their calendar year salary as contribution to research time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These salary funds are not substitutional (cannot be used to relieve a university of salary costs) and cannot be used to reduce teaching loads below the departmental norm. They can only be used to supplement salary, similar to a U.S. summer salary. For non-U.S. requests, the salary request must not violate institutional policies about effort exceeding 100% per year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect cost limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect costs are limited to 20 percent of applicable direct costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This cap is outlined in the Simons Foundation grant policies; applicants should compute indirect costs accordingly and consult policies for details on applicable direct costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel salary support allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Salary support and related benefits, including tuition support, are allowable for staff/research scientists, postdoctoral fellows and research associates, graduate students or undergraduate research assistants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All personnel requesting salary should be entered and justified in the budget. Do not combine multiple personnel on one budget line; each person (e.g., each postdoc) must be itemized individually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel, visitors, and conference support
rubrics_metrics.description: Domestic or international travel for the PI(s), co-Investigator(s) and students, support for visitors and collaborators (travel, meals, lodging), and conferences/working meetings (including participant travel, lodging, meals, vehicle rentals and facility fees) are allowable expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include appropriate justification in the budget for travel and meeting costs. Travel-related items (parking, hotel, registration, taxi) are explicitly allowed when appropriate to project needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research equipment and consumables
rubrics_metrics.description: Research equipment, experiments, computations, supplies and other expenses directly related to the research, including computers, computer support, professional literature, publication expenses and professional membership dues, are allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify equipment and supply purchases in the budget justification. Assume purchases must be directly related to the proposed project.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI and co-Investigator eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs and co-Investigators (co-Is) must hold a tenured or tenure-track faculty, or equivalent, position at institutions or centers at the time of application and for the duration of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no restrictions on department or discipline; PIs/co-Is may be from non-U.S. institutions. A co-I must be employed by or affiliated with a PI institution or another participating organization under a consortium agreement. Adjunct faculty are not eligible to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simons Foundation employee restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Simons Foundation employees who receive a W-2 from the Simons Foundation, including employees of the Flatiron Institute, may not apply as a PI to any Simons Foundation or Simons Foundation International RFAs released by the Simons Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIs and any project personnel listed who will receive funding for salary, travel, support for students/postdocs/research staff, lab equipment, computing time or other individual expenses may not be employees of the Simons Foundation or Flatiron Institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional eligibility and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be submitted by established U.S. and foreign public and private educational institutions and stand-alone research centers. For-profit institutions are not eligible to receive grant funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding to U.S. national labs or salary support of scientists employed at these labs is not allowed (lab scientists may be non-funded project members; travel/local expenses allowed). SF and SFI do not provide funding to institutions in China (including Hong Kong), nor to fiscal sponsors/agents of institutions in China/Hong Kong; this includes subcontracts or consultants residing/working for institutions in China/Hong Kong.

rubrics_metrics.name: LOI submission via SAM and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit a Letter of Intent (LOI) via the Simons Award Manager (SAM). The deadline is rolling; an LOI can be submitted at any time. Applicants will be notified of a decision within three months of the LOI submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If LOI is approved, the applicant will be invited to submit a full proposal; full proposal deadline will be provided in LOI notification and will be no sooner than three months from LOI approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: LOI content and formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: LOI Narrative: two-page limit, plus up to one page for references and figures (which can be embedded). The LOI must be signed by the main PI on letterhead and include a brief summary of support requested, names of other PIs if applicable, scientific goals, background relevant to the application and a brief budget justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attachments should be single spaced and in typeface no smaller than 10-point font. Margins, in all directions, must be at least one-half inch.

rubrics_metrics.name: LOI attachments: budget and biosketch format
rubrics_metrics.description: LOI requires a Budget (one-page limit) and Personnel Biosketches for each PI and co-Investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget should be a tentative yearly budget indicating total amounts, major expense categories and proposed start and end dates. Biosketches must be in SciENcv, NIH, or NSF-style format or a two- to three-page CV. File naming conventions: LastName_FirstName_Biosketch (and similar for publications/support PDFs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Full proposal narrative and attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Full Proposal Narrative: six-page limit, plus up to two pages for references and figures (which can be embedded). Upload personnel biosketches and other required files via SAM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full proposal must be submitted via SAM by the main PI and institution. Full proposals include start/end dates, budgets up to five years, publications and other support documentation. Applicants must indicate whether any PI/personnel are affiliated with Simons/Flatiron as Visiting Scholar/Independent Contractor/Employee. Generative AI disclosure is required in both LOI and full proposal (indicate extent and how it was used).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget preparation and justification rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Budgets are entered in SAM for up to five years in U.S. dollars. Enter each PI on each proposal in the Personnel Costs section even if not requesting salary. Provide justification for each budget line item entered, including all Personnel Costs requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not combine personnel on one budget line (e.g., multiple postdocs must be itemized individually). An insufficient budget justification will result in the proposal not being considered further. Notes about SAM: copying budgets between years can duplicate entries; duplicated entries must be individually deleted. For projects with more than one PI at different institutions, all but one of the budgets should be entered as a subcontract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project personnel definitions and SAM role rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Project personnel include individuals who contribute to the scientific development or execution of a project in a substantive, measurable way, whether or not they request salaries or compensation. The Simons Foundation does not use the role type 'co-PI'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For additional PIs, add them as 'Subcontract Personnel' or 'Project Personnel' in SAM in the appropriate role (e.g., 'Subcontract Lead – With or Without Application Access' or 'Project Personnel – With or Without Application Access'), then use 'Add More Detail' to select Additional Principal Investigator. To appear in budget dropdowns, personnel must be added in the Contacts & Personnel tab and assigned an application role; close and reopen the budget for changes to populate. Do not select 'TBD' if personnel are known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications and Other Support requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications: provide a list of up to 10 relevant publications for each PI and co-I via PDF upload or SAM profiles. Other Support: provide current and pending support for each PI and co-I via PDF upload or SAM profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If providing Other Support via SAM profile, reporting overlap is required to submit an application (while overlap is not a consideration for funding in this program, click 'Report Overlap' and select Yes or No). If using PDF upload, NSF or other format is sufficient and should provide award number, source, title, dates and total costs. File naming conventions: LastName_FirstName_Publications and LastName_FirstName_Support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission, sign-off, and institutional signature rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For LOI stage, institutional sign-off is not required. For full proposals, the applicant sends for sign-off; the Signing Official must provide an electronic signature in the Submission tab of the proposal and click 'Submit Signature' to submit to the foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the application is signed, the Signing Official, applicant, and Financial Officer will receive notifications. You cannot submit if the deadline has passed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application limits, resubmission and award recipient
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no limit to the number of applications per PI or institution, and applicants may reapply if not awarded. The grant is awarded to the applicant's institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that institution (not individual) receives award and plan institutional processes accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on fields and eligibility (subject areas)
rubrics_metrics.description: At this time, proposals in the chemistry field are not eligible for consideration under this program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm topical fit before applying; the program emphasizes theory in mathematics, physics and computer science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must indicate the extent to which, if any, generative AI technology was used and how it was used to develop the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disclosure is required for both LOI and full proposal submissions.
